originalRequest: i want you to draft the redesign of the overall appearance of the browser
subject: Drift, an Electron desktop web browser (React renderer). The request covers the browser's own chrome and interface, not a marketing site.
scope: Visual redesign of the whole browser chrome and its built-in surfaces, kept to the current features and structure: window frame and topbar, vertical tab sidebar, address bar, overlays and panels, and the new-tab page. No new browser features, and no changes to the main-process logic.
primaryGoal: Give Drift a cohesive, distinctive and polished look across every surface so it feels like one calm, premium product instead of a set of separately styled panels, while web content stays the main focus.
audience: Everyday desktop users who browse for long sessions and manage many tabs and workspaces, including people switching from Chrome, Edge or Arc (Drift has a browser import flow).
offer: A focused, glassy, sidebar-first browser with workspaces, split view, a compact mode, built-in Shields, a password manager and extension support.
primaryAction: Browse: find, switch and open tabs, and type into the address bar with as little visual friction as possible.
creativeControl: High. The user asked for a draft redesign of the overall look, so the visual direction is delegated, within the existing feature set and the Ember highlight convention.
requiredContent: Window frame and topbar: auto-hiding topbar (40px, 220ms slide), custom window controls, a hot zone that reveals it, and a content shadow around the web view

Vertical tab sidebar: workspace label and switcher, rail search, essentials drop zone, pinned tabs, tab rows (favicon, title, audio indicator, close), new-tab button, sidebar pin and menu triggers, resize handle
Address bar: URL pill and capsule with security state, bookmark star, loading spinner and error state
Compact mode: compact edge and hover preview of the sidebar when it is collapsed
Split view: divider, per-pane focus state and split-close control
Browser menu and sidebar menu: dropdown and overlay styling
Find bar: in-page search with match count and next/previous controls

Overlay panels and dialogs: Settings, Downloads, Passwords (including Drift-styled password prompts), Shields, Extensions and extension actions, Workspaces, Updates, Default browser and Browser import
New-tab page: search entry and the workspace or wallpaper backdrop (--wallpaper-image)
States across all surfaces: hover, active or selected tab, focus rings, loading, error, disabled and empty states
Motion: useful transitions for topbar reveal, sidebar collapse and expand, tab open, close and reorder, panel and dialog open and close, split view and the find bar
constraints: Must be implementable as CSS-token and stylesheet changes in src/renderer/style.css plus small TSX class changes, with the current component structure and features kept as they are
Contrast UI (progress, on-states, selected and active) uses the --highlight Ember token rather than the grey or purple accent (project convention)
Keep keyboard focus visibility and accessible contrast; tab and control hit targets no smaller than the current 32px control size
Web page content must stay visually dominant; chrome should not compete with it
Bundled fonts only (Inter Variable, Bricolage variable width, Junicode italic); no new remote font dependencies
brandInputs: Colors (src/renderer/style.css): --accent #5856d6 (indigo), --text #1d1d1f, --muted #69696e, --chrome-bg/--backdrop #eef0f5, --surface #ffffff, --border #d2d2d7, --error #d70015, glass layers #ffffff8c, #ffffffd9 and edge #ffffffb3 with a 24px blur, and indigo-tinted shadows
Ember --highlight token for contrast UI (project memory)
Typography: Inter Variable as the UI font; Bricolage Grotesque (variable width) and Junicode Italic are also bundled in src/renderer/fonts
Shape and motion: --radius 12px, --tab-height 34px, --control-size 32px, --topbar 40px, ease cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1) and ease-out cubic-bezier(0.33,1,0.68,1)
Current visual style: light, translucent, frosted-glass chrome in a macOS-like idiom, with hairline borders and soft shadows
assumptions: 'The browser' means the Drift app's own interface (chrome, sidebar, panels, new-tab page), so pageType is dashboard with screens rather than marketing sections
This is a draft direction for review, keeping current layout regions and features; no new functionality is planned
No dark theme exists in the stylesheet today; the redesign defines light as the primary theme and also plans a matching dark token set, because people browse for long sessions
The Inter, Bricolage and Junicode fonts stay available; the design picks among them
Interface transitions are included because no request for no animation was given
unresolved: Whether the indigo --accent should be kept, retuned or replaced next to Ember
Whether a dark theme should ship together with the light redesign or later
